item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact required Upload signature and explicitly tests multipart encoding, retry behavior, validation, and source-reader failures. Neither patch is merge-ready because both bypass FilesService.Add and add forbidden association machinery.","reasons":["B implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces UploadFileOption, breaking the specified API and preventing reuse of existing FilesOption values.","B covers all required test categories, including source-reader error propagation. A has no visible source-reader failure test.","B preserves Files.Add implementation and retry machinery, while A makes a broad, explicitly out-of-scope RawClient retry change for arbitrary io.ReadSeeker bodies.","B passes existing query and request options into Upload. A's separate option system omits existing FilesOption query behavior and duplicates request-option handling under a new API."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong option type and therefore violates the exact public API contract.","It adds numerous forbidden association options and a duplicate upload-specific option framework.","It calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request and response behavior and omitting existing FilesOption query handling of Add APIs; routing through Add is the contract requirement to centralize behavior, even though this duplication resembles the current implementation closely enough to pass gates and tests now. It creates maintenance drift risk if Add changes later because the duplicate path would not automatically inherit those changes. A also expands retry machinery in RawClient in direct conflict with the required scope discipline, potentially changing retry and body-lifecycle semantics for every raw request. Its GetBody closure shares and mutates one seeker, which is less robust than independent replay readers and may be unsafe under unusual transport reuse. It introduces NewForm rather than directly reusing internal/multipartbody.NewFile, and adds capabilities the contract explicitly excludes. It lacks a visible test for propagating source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["It calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's option, request, decoding, and error logic.","It adds forbidden association fields and WithFile*ID APIs; comments incorrectly claim these options associate files uploaded with Add, but Add never consumes cfg.form.","It extends multipartbody with NewFileWithFields and invokes that instead of using the required NewFile helper directly, adding unnecessary machinery driven by out-of-scope associations."]}
